clue.text: Refined weapon, good for engagement

indicators.note: engagement read as being engaged or held, so the weapon's letters take in the next piece

parts.note: a cutlass is a short curved sword

explanation.surface: A sophisticated sword, just the thing for a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' pretends to mean a fight, but it signals one piece held inside the other. Cut-glass describes a very upper-class British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a cut-glass accent or manner is precise, polished and upper-class.

clue.text: Bird shaking off tail, freezing

indicators.note: losing its tail means the bird name drops its final letter

parts.note: the bittern is a heron-like marsh bird

explanation.surface: A bird in icy weather ruffles and loses its tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: bitter weather is bitingly cold, so freezing fits.

clue.text: Collecting a heavy weight, send giants to rebuild megalith

indicators.note: the rearranged letters gather up the weight, holding it within them
rebuilding the words means putting their letters back together in a new order

parts.note: a ton is a heavy unit of weight

explanation.surface: An order to send giants off to reconstruct a great stone monument, lifting a huge mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rebuild' rearranges SEND GIANTS into STANDINGSE, and 'Collecting' puts TON inside it before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a megalith is a great prehistoric stone, typically one set upright in the ground.

clue.text: Strong drink, two rupees

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
R is an abbreviation for rupee or rupees

explanation.surface: A stiff drink costing a couple of rupees.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bracer is a reviving alcoholic drink, a pick-me-up.

clue.text: Having sealed off old pub, takes to court winning evidence?

indicators.note: sealing something off encloses it, so the court verb wraps round the other letters

parts.note: to try someone is to take them to court for trial
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: Someone shuts down an old pub and sues, hoping to win the case.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: cups and medals are trophies, physical evidence that someone won.

clue.text: Hazy, perhaps, like a hanging mist?

explanation.surface: Fog suspended above, unclear and vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a plan up in the air is undecided, hazy; a hanging mist is literally aloft.

clue.text: Winning round ends in short shot — this?

definitions.text: Winning round ends in short shot — this?

indicators.note: turned round means the letters for winning are read backwards

parts.note: one up in golf or a match means winning, so up

indicators.note: the ends of these two words supply their last letters

explanation.surface: A golfer wonders whether a short stroke will win the round.
explanation.definitionFit: A putt is the short stroke on the green that can finish and win a golf hole.

clue.text: Pretty average entertainment

definitions.meaning: a funfair or fete with rides and stalls

explanation.surface: A show that was only moderately entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple sense: beautiful, middling in quality, and a fete or funfair.

clue.text: Cry, sobbing uncontrollably, gentle voice long gone

indicators.note: sobbing out of control jumbles the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Weeping hard for a soft voice that has fallen silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Bing Crosby (died 1977) was the great American crooner, hence the gentle voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Crosby's soft crooning style made him the classic gentle singing voice, now dead.

clue.text: Soldier like Frenchman, for example

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
dig is slang for like or appreciate
M is the abbreviation of Monsieur

explanation.surface: A soldier who resembles a Frenchman, say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' looks like a comparison but is the verb, as in 'I dig it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a paradigm is a model or typical instance, so an example.

clue.text: Wet politician in power

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: sway is power or influence, as in holding sway
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A feeble politician holding office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' suggests a British political insult for a weak moderate, but here it means boggy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: swampy ground is waterlogged and soggy.

clue.text: Masseur put his foot down, being officially sanctioned

parts.note: a masseur rubs clients, so is a rubber
stamped means brought the foot down hard

explanation.surface: A masseur, once licensed, laid down the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a rubber-stamped decision is officially approved, often as a formality.

clue.text: Legendary woman, long-distance runner

definitions.meaning: a female warrior of Greek myth
a river runs, and this South American one is vast

explanation.surface: A mythical woman who is also a marathon athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the warrior women of Greek legend and the South American river, a very long runner.

clue.text: Advertising method thus dropped, extremes of tastelessness contained

parts.note: so means thus or in this way

indicators.note: the fall verb holds the next letters within it

parts.note: fell means dropped, the past of fall

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An advertising approach so lacking in taste that it was abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a soft sell is gentle, low-pressure persuasion in advertising.

clue.text: Loose nuts screwed up, then hit

indicators.note: screwed up means muddled, so the letters of the word are jumbled

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply

explanation.surface: Loose nuts get tightened, then struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' is a verb here: to set free.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to unstrap something is to unfasten or release it, as loose means to set free.

clue.text: Island prison captivated by relative singing in an opera

indicators.note: held captive, so the jail is enclosed by the other letters

parts.note: gran is a grandmother
an aria is a solo song in an opera
can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A grandmother entranced by an operatic performance, prisoner of the music.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Gran Canaria is one of Spain's Canary Islands.

clue.text: Guts of male climbing cherry tree

indicators.note: the guts are the inner letters of the word
in a down clue, climbing means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: cherry red is a colour, so cherry gives red

explanation.surface: A man's insides as he climbs a cherry tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the alder is a waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Singer not entirely conscious in a trance

indicators.note: only part of these words is used, the letters running within them

explanation.surface: A vocalist, half awake, in a dreamlike state.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Frank Sinatra was the famous American singer.

clue.text: See one store in brownish-red, unfinished

indicators.note: these letters go inside the colour
the colour word loses its last letter

parts.note: brick red is a brownish-red colour
I is the Roman numeral one
a shop is a store

explanation.surface: A colour note: picture a single shop in rusty red, half-painted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not a command but a noun, a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a see is a bishop's diocese, his bishopric.

clue.text: Chinese path where grass comes up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A Chinese trail where grass sprouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Translation: Tao means the way or path in Chinese philosophy.

clue.text: Part of kettle for water perhaps?

definitions.meaning: the heating coil inside an electric kettle
water was one of the four classical building blocks with earth, air and fire

explanation.surface: The bit of a kettle that heats the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the heating coil in a kettle, and water as one of the ancient four constituents.

clue.text: Where wallowers at home when studying part of the brain?

parts.note: hippos wallow in mud and water; hippo serves as the word
a campus is where students live and study

explanation.surface: Asking where wallowing creatures would live if they were students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where' just introduces the playful picture of hippos at university.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippocampus is a structure in the brain's temporal lobe involved in memory.

clue.text: Man unusually in front of a train? An islander

parts.words: Man unusually in front of a train?
parts.note: a bride walks in front of her train, so a male one would be unusual: he plus bride
taken as written

explanation.surface: An islander wonders about a man standing oddly ahead of a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: The train is a wedding dress train, not a railway one. The Hebrides are islands off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Hebridean is a native of the Hebrides, Scottish isles.

clue.text: This paper's theme adapted for The Times, perhaps?

definitions.text: This paper's theme adapted for The Times, perhaps?

parts.words: This paper's theme adapted for The Times, perhaps?
parts.note: a crossword's stock device is a word whose letters are reordered to make another, as 'The Times' could be reworked into a new phrase

explanation.surface: An editor's note on a theme reworked for the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted for' suggests editing, but describes a word made from rearranged letters, the very device this clue type names.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a reordering of letters to form new words is exactly what the word names.

clue.text: Undoing last bits of thin rope, me and sibling

indicators.note: the final letters of these two words

parts.note: sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: Our downfall: the frayed end of a thin rope, me and my sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one's nemesis is the agent of one's downfall, so one's undoing.

clue.text: Able to stand blood pressure initially, ideal to exercise

indicators.note: exercising works things over, so the letters are rearranged
the first letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Exercise is ideal for blood pressure, if you can stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipedal creatures walk on two legs, so can stand upright.

clue.text: Stick man?

definitions.meaning: to man something is to provide it with people, a verb

explanation.surface: A stick figure drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a walking stick or pole, and the verb meaning to provide with personnel.

clue.text: Not entirely a fool, nineteenth-century author

indicators.note: the word for a fool is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a bozo is a stupid person

explanation.surface: A Victorian writer who was something of an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Boz was Charles Dickens's early pen name, as in Sketches by Boz.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Boz was the pseudonym Dickens used for his first sketches in the 1830s.
